title: A depth-aware 100 km limit kept all 35 large seven-day follow-up pairs around deep M 6.5-7.4 anchors in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether surface-distance windows overstate large nearby follow-up occurrence around deep earthquakes. We used a fixed USGS ComCat snapshot for 2000-2025. Anchors had preferred magnitude from 6.5 to less than 7.5. Follow-up events had magnitude at least 5.5. At 100 km and seven days, a distance rule that adds depth separation kept all 35 follow-up pairs around 110 deep anchors at depth at least 300 km. Both rules gave 21 anchors with one or more follow-up events. The depth-aware rule removed four of eight pairs around intermediate-depth anchors. Deep occurrence was 19.1%, compared with 48.1% for shallow anchors after magnitude standardization. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for the deep-minus-shallow difference was -36.5 to -21.2 percentage points. Other distance and time windows removed some deep pairs. Thus the primary geometry result has a limited scope. It does not show that depth separation never matters or explain physical triggering. Mixed magnitude types, shared events, tectonic differences, source revisions and a fixed large-event floor limit inference. Code, aggregate results, source provenance, independent count checks and a figure are included. External source records and event-level transformations remain outside the package.

display.caption: Large follow-up occurrence under surface and depth-aware distance limits. Anchors have M 6.5-7.4. Follow-up events have M at least 5.5. Left: the primary 100 km, seven-day window. Right: deep occurrence minus shallow occurrence standardized to deep magnitude bins. Bars show conditional 95% three-year calendar-block intervals. These intervals do not include catalog or tectonic uncertainty.

citations.reason: Published spatial-summary audit motivated a separate global distance-window comparison. No source data or code were reused.
Exact fixed snapshot is identified by hash in provenance.json. Raw and event-level derived records are external.
